title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20
source: This is a restored version of shind: 97364; MR > R (Buddy Miller) HEAVILY EDITED > R @ 71/2ips (Will Boswell) > CD; Transfer info: reel > AKAI GX625 > Apogee Mini Me (24/96) > Apogee Mini Dac (monitoring) > Wavelab 5.0 (dithered to 16/44) > CD > EAC > Wav > Flac16Restoration completed with Diamond Cut Forensics 10.2.

ai_review.summary: A standout acoustic show with great performances (especially “Caution”) but captured on a stealth‑rig audience source that has modest balance and clarity issues.
ai_review.review: Reviewers rave about the quality of the music – the acoustic set, Phil Lesh’s solid bass work and the superb rendition of “Caution” are highlighted as superior to many other 1970 shows. The recording comes from a hidden stage rig, so while it avoids major drop‑outs, listeners note minor imperfections, occasional warble fixes, and an uneven mix that tames Pigpen’s harp/vocals while pushing the organ forward.

ai_rating.rationale: The show receives enthusiastic 5‑star praise for performance, especially acoustic numbers, but multiple reviewers flag recording balance and clarity problems, pulling the overall rating down to a solid 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stealth‑rig audience taping with occasional location changes; minor audio imperfections noted, warbled middle sections improved versus other sources, but Pigpen's harp/vocals are reduced and organ is unnaturally boosted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set praised for its smooth flow; improved transition into “Caution” highlighted, overall pacing described as excellent despite the lack of detailed song list.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh is noted to be on bass and performing solidly in this acoustic setting.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ work is unusually prominent in this mix, likely due to the recording’s processing.
